newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian drug lord gets 28 years for kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug lord gets 28 years for kidnapping.

text.p: A leading member of Colombia's Cali drug cartel was sentenced to 28 years in prison on Tuesday for a kidnapping carried out in 1992, judicial officials said.

A statement issued by court officials in Cali, the southwest city that gave the powerful drug cartel its name, said the 28-year sentence for Phanor Arizabaleta was the maximum possible under Colombian law.
It was also the stiffest meted out yet to any member of the Cali drug mob, most of whose leaders were arrested during a nationwide crackdown on the criminal drug syndicate in 1995.

It was handed down by a so-called "faceless" or anonymous judge in Cali where Arizabaleta is housed in the maximum security wing of the Palmira prison. The identity of scores of judges working across Colombia is hidden from the public to shield them from assassination or kidnapping attempts by the country's notoriously violent drug gangs.

Arizabaleta, considered the fifth top man in the Cali cartel hierarchy, surrendered to police in July 1995. Kidnapping charges were filed against him three months later stemming from the June 1992 abduction of Harold Alfonso Barbosa.
The court statement said Arizabaleta ordered the kidnapping so that Barbosa's sister, a resident of Toronto, Canada, would make good on a $200,000 debt.
Arizabaleta has not yet been sentenced on drug charges. Under legislation approved in February that stiffened penalities sharply, he could face up to 60 years for narcotics trafficking.

The new legislation, which did not take effect retroactively, came too late for brothers Gilberto and Miguel Rodriguez Orejuela, the main leaders of the Cali cartel. The two were sentenced to short prison sentences on Jan. 17 that could see them walk free in as little as five years.
